10845               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10846               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10847               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10848               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10849               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10850               	; 	' away from.
10851               	; 	'
10852               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10853               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10854               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10855               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10856               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10857               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10858               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10859               	; 	'
10860               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10861               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10862               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10863               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10864               	; 	'
10865               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10866               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10867               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10868               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10869               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10870               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10871               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10872               	; 	' hit sound; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10873               	; 	'
10874               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10875               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.

11038               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as

11043               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
11044               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the

12234               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12235               	; 	' ======================================================================
12236               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12237               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12238               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12239               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12240               	; 	'
12241               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12242               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12243               	; 	'
12244               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12245               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12246               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12247               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12248               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12249               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12250               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered

12252               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12253               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12254               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.

12281               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12282               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12283               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12284               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12285               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12286               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12287               	; 	'

12289               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12290               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12291               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12292               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12293               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12294               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12308               	; 	#if NES
12309               	; 	' A VBLANK OF ITS OWN, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE-SCREEN FLASH.
12310               	; 	'
12311               	; 	' PPUBUF is not flushed when it is written -- it ACCUMULATES for the whole
12312               	; 	' pass and the NMI empties it in one go, so every VPOKE the radar makes,
12313               	; 	' every HUD digit and this upload all land in the SAME vblank. And the
12314               	; 	' handler's copy loop does not stop when vblank ends: it runs to the end of
12315               	; 	' the descriptor and then writes PPUADDR and both PPUSCROLLs, which
12316               	; 	' mid-frame re-points the PPU's own render address. The rest of that frame
12317               	; 	' is drawn from the wrong place. On screen that is not a dropped tile, it
12318               	; 	' is the ENTIRE PICTURE jumping for a frame -- which is what has been
12319               	; 	' reported, repeatedly, as the screen flashing on an escalator.
12320               	; 	'
12321               	; 	' The arithmetic says it cannot be anything else. NTSC vblank is about
12322               	; 	' 2273 CPU cycles; NMI entry, the flicker test and OAM DMA spend ~560 of
12323               	; 	' them before a single byte is copied. A copy descriptor costs ~50 cycles
12324               	; 	' plus 14 a byte, so these six characters -- 96 bytes, because a tile is
12325               	; 	' SIXTEEN bytes in two bitplanes, not eight -- are ~1400 on their own.
12326               	; 	' That leaves about 270 cycles, or SIX single-byte pokes, for everything
12327               	; 	' else the pass queued. The radar alone beats that whenever a dot moves.
12328               	; 	'
12329               	; 	' Nothing smaller fixes it, because the overrun is per FRAME, not per
12330               	; 	' second: slowing the animation down just makes the bad frames rarer.
12331               	; 	' Splitting the six characters across two frames tears the staircase, and
12332               	; 	' only three of the six have a constant second bitplane, so dropping a
12333               	; 	' plane does not buy a frame's worth either. What DOES work is giving the
12334               	; 	' upload a vblank with nothing else in it: this WAIT flushes the pass's
12335               	; 	' radar and HUD writes, and the descriptor queued below is then almost all
12336               	; 	' the next vblank has to carry -- ~1960 cycles of 2273, inside the window
12337               	; 	' with room to spare.
12338               	; 	'
12339               	; 	' IT COSTS ONE FRAME A PASS, on the two screens that carry a flight and
12340               	; 	' nowhere else -- esc_tick has already returned on the other six. The
12341               	; 	' rider is paced from the animation rather than from the frame delta (see
12342               	; 	' below), so a slower pass slows the ride too and the two cannot drift.
12343               	; 	WAIT
12344               	; 	#endif

12348               	; 	' direction is ever on screen: screen 0 carries a west flight and screen

12352               	; 	' `define_char`, which in bitmap mode is LDIRVM3 -- the TRIPLE copy, once

12355               	; 	'

12691               	;
12692               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12693               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12694               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12695               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12696               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12697               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12698               	; 	'
12699               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12700               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12701               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12702               	; 	'
12703               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12704               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12705               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12706               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12707               	; 	'
12708               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12709               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12710               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12711               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12712               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12713               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12714               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12715               	; 	'
12716               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12717               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12718               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12719               	; 	'
12720               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12721               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12722               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

13040               	; 	' THE ONE READ-MODIFY-WRITE ON THE PATTERN TABLE. The radar ORs a

13165               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out

13168               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
13169               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
13170               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).

13173               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13174               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13175               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13176               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13177               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
13178               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
13179               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
13180               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
13181               	; 	'
13182               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
13183               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
13184               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
13185               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
13186               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
13187               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
13188               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on

13191               	; 	'
13192               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
13193               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
13194               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
13195               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
13196               	; 	'

13834               	;
13835               	; #if NES
13836               	; 	' ----------------------------------------------------------------------
13837               	; 	' Attributes select a palette per 16x16 quadrant. gennescolor.py derives
13838               	; 	' eight screen tables; draw_screen stages one in nesb, masks fixtures,
13839               	; 	' then uploads all 64 bytes through nes_attrs_put within one vblank.
13840               	; 	' A MESSAGE BOX GOES GOLD ON DARK BLUE, and the caller says which four
13841               	; 	' bytes in #nav.
13842               	; 	'
13843               	; 	' The text's paper is index 1 and its ink index 3 (see the font upload);
13844               	; 	' over the store those are P0's green and gold -- the same green the box is
13845               	; 	' sitting on, which is what made the messages hard to read. P1 is the HUD's
13846               	; 	' palette, dark blue and gold, so pointing the box's attribute bytes at it
13847               	; 	' gives a message the same treatment as the score line.
13848               	; 	'
13849               	; 	' FOUR BYTES AND NOT ONE MORE. An attribute byte covers four characters by
13850               	; 	' four, and the box is sized and placed to cover exactly four of them
13851               	; 	' (gentitle.py BOX_ROW/BOX_COL/BOX_W): byte columns 2..5, which is name
13852               	; 	' columns 8..23. Anything wider would recolour shop floor beside the box.
13853               	; 	'
13854               	; 	' THIS IS A ROUTINE BECAUSE IT WAS WRITTEN OUT TWICE AND MISSED A THIRD
13855               	; 	' TIME. GOT HIM! kept the store's colours while the other boxes changed,
13856               	; 	' and nothing failed -- it is a readable message in the wrong palette.
13857               	; 	' checkmsg.py now fails the build if a message box is drawn without one of
13858               	; 	' these beside it.
13859               	; 	'
13860               	; 	' Nothing puts them back, because nothing needs to: every path out of a
13861               	; 	' message box redraws the screen, and draw_screen calls nes_attr, which
13862               	; 	' rewrites all sixty-four.
13863               	; nes_boxatt:
13864               	; 	WAIT
13865               	; 	IF #nav = 9178 THEN
13866               	; 		' GAME OVER begins in the lower half of one attribute row.
13867               	; 		' Preserve the surrounding halves from the actual screen upload.
13868               	; 		FOR nai = 0 TO 3
13869               	; 			nink = (nmsg(nai) AND 15) OR 80
13870               	; 			VPOKE #nav,nink
13871               	; 			#nsrc = #nav + 8
13872               	; 			nink = (nmsg(nai) AND 240) OR 15
13873               	; 			VPOKE #nsrc,nink
13874               	; 			#nav = #nav + 1
13875               	; 		NEXT nai
13876               	; 		#nsrc = 8712		' PPU row 16 col 8, bottom border
13877               	; 	ELSE
13878               	; 		' Skyline P1/P2 split: retain every colour outside the box.
13879               	; 		FOR nai = 0 TO 3
13880               	; 			VPOKE #nav,165
13881               	; 			#nav = #nav + 1
13882               	; 		NEXT nai
13883               	; 		#nsrc = 8392		' PPU row 6 col 8, bottom border
13884               	; 	END IF
13885               	; 	FOR nai = 0 TO 15
13886               	; 		VPOKE #nsrc,CH_ECAR
13887               	; 		#nsrc = #nsrc + 1
13888               	; 	NEXT nai
13889               	; 	WAIT
13890               	; 	RETURN
13891               	;
13892               	; nes_attr:
13893               	; 	' nesb holds attributes only during draw_screen; flush before reuse by
13894               	; 	' escalator or marquee CHR uploads. One 64-byte copy fits one vblank.

14375               	;
14376               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
14377               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
14378               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
14379               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
14380               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
14381               	; 	'
14382               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
14383               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
14384               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
14385               	; 	'
14386               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
14387               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
14388               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
14389               	; 	'
14390               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
14391               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
14392               	; 	'
14393               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
14394               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
14395               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
14396               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
14397               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
14398               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
14399               	; 	'
14400               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
14401               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
14402               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
14403               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
14404               	; 	'
14405               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
14406               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
14407               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
14408               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)

14552               	;
14553               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14554               	; 	'
14555               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14556               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14557               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14558               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14559               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14560               	; 	'
14561               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14562               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14563               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14564               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14565               	; 	' counting stops.
14566               	;
14567               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14568               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14569               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14570               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14571               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14572               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14573               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14574               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14575               	; 	'
14576               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14577               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14578               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
14579               	;

14623               	; 	' THE CAST IS NOT TAKEN AWAY YET -- hide_all now runs AFTER the beat.
14624               	; 	'
14625               	; 	' It used to run here, so the moment the clock emptied, Harry and the
14626               	; 	' thing that had just hit him vanished and the sound played over an empty
14627               	; 	' store. The hit that ENDS a round is the worst case: `do_hit` sets tout
14628               	; 	' before the freeze starts and the main loop leaves on the very next pass,
14629               	; 	' so the hit sound gets one tick and everything is already gone.
14630               	; 	'
14631               	; 	' The pause drains the sound; leaving the actors up means it drains over
14632               	; 	' the picture that caused it. Nothing is moving -- the pause ticks sfx_tick
14633               	; 	' and nothing else -- so it is a held tableau, not a frozen game.
14634               	; 	' THE MESSAGE BOX, ON THE GAME SCREEN AND NOT INSTEAD OF IT.
14635               	; 	'
14636               	; 	' It used to CLS before GAME OVER, so the last thing the player saw was
14637               	; 	' the store being deleted and then two words on an empty field -- which
14638               	; 	' reads as the program ending rather than as the game ending. The store
14639               	; 	' stays; the message sits in the middle of it.
14640               	; 	'
14641               	; 	' THE BOX IS THE FONT'S OWN BACKGROUND. Every font character is black on
14642               	; 	' HUD_BG (dark blue), so a row of SPACES is a solid dark blue bar. A blank
14643               	; 	' row above and below the text is a frame for the price of two strings and
14644               	; 	' no new characters, and it reads against the store because nothing else on
14645               	; 	' the playfield is that colour.
14646               	; 	'
14647               	; 	' THIRTEEN WIDE, WHICH IS THE LONGEST MESSAGE PLUS ONE EITHER SIDE.
14648               	; 	' HE GOT AWAY and THE BIPLANE are both eleven. Every string below is padded
14649               	; 	' to exactly thirteen so the box has straight edges, and column 10 puts it
14650               	; 	' at columns 10-22 -- centre 16, the screen's.
14651               	; 	'
14652               	; 	' THE REASON IS ALWAYS ON THE SAME ROW, and that is what lets one layout
14653               	; 	' serve both cases. Losing a life draws three rows around it; losing the
14654               	; 	' last one draws two more ON TOP, so GAME OVER appears above the reason
14655               	; 	' rather than replacing it. Printing the reason at a different row for each
14656               	; 	' case would need `PRINT AT` with a variable, and every other PRINT in this
14657               	; 	' program uses a constant.
14658               	; 	#if NES
14659               	; 	' FLUSH THE PASS BEFORE DRAWING A BOX. PPUBUF accumulates for a whole loop
14660               	; 	' pass and is emptied by one NMI, so a message box -- sixty-four cells,

14930               	;
14931               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14932               	; 	'
14933               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14934               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14935               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14936               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14937               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14938               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14939               	; 	'
14940               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14941               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14942               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14943               	; 	'
14944               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14945               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14946               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14947               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14948               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14949               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14950               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14951               	; 	'
14952               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14953               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14954               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14955               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14956               	; 	'
14957               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14958               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14959               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14960               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14961               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14962               	; 	'
14963               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14964               	; 	' did not finish.
14965               	; pause_beat:
14966               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

15015               	; 	' SOUND
15016               	; 	' ======================================================================
15017               	; 	' Every effect gets an explicit note-off. SOUND latches -- with no
15018               	; 	' `SOUND ch,f,0` the last tone sustains for ever. And the second argument
15019               	; 	' is a 10-BIT DIVISOR, max 1023: SMALLER IS HIGHER, so a rising sweep is
15020               	; 	' written as a falling number and anything over 1023 is silently masked
15021               	; 	' to an unrelated pitch.

15025               	; 	' biplane; they share the warbler, so sharing its trigger costs three
15026               	; 	' fewer statements -- and the fixed area was 14 bytes OVER when they were
15027               	; 	' written separately. Nothing else sets sfj, and if a jump and a plane
15028               	; 	' landed in one pass the last writer would win, which is academic: the
15029               	; 	' plane ends the round.

15404               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
15405               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
15406               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
15407               	;
15408               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
15409               	; 	'
15410               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
15411               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
15412               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
15413               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
15414               	; 	'
15415               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
15416               	; 	'
15417               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
15418               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
15419               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
15420               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
15421               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
15422               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
15423               	; 	'
15424               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
15425               	; 	'
15426               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
15427               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
15428               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
15429               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
15430               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
15431               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
15432               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
15433               	; 	'
15434               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
15435               	; 	'
15436               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
15437               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
15438               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
15439               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
15440               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
15441               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
15442               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
15443               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
15444               	; 	'
15445               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
15446               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
15447               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
15448               	; 	'
15449               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
15450               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
15451               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
15452               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
15453               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
15454               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
15455               	; 	'
15456               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
15457               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
15458               	; 	'
15459               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
15460               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
15461               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
15462               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
15463               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
15464               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
15465               	; 	'
15466               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
15467               	; 	'
15468               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
15469               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
15470               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
15471               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
15472               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
15473               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
15474               	; 	' back to 7.

     F85E D000

     F862 AE2A

15771 F866 C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
15772 F868 0450  20 	b *r0
15773               	;
15774               	; 	' A catch must not erase a life awarded on the same gameplay pass.
15775               	; life_finish:
15776               cvb_LIFE_FINISH
15777               	; 	GOSUB life_tick
15778 F86A 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     F86C AE2A     
15779 F86E F786     	data cvb_LIFE_TICK
15780               	; 	IF spt = 0 THEN RETURN
15781 F870 D020  34 	movb @cvb_SPT,r0
     F872 224E     
15782 F874 1602  14 	jne cv1019 ; shortened jeq / b
15783               	; removed long branch (shortbranches.py)
15784               cv1020
15785 F876 C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
15786 F878 0450  20 	b *r0
15787               cv1019
15788               	; 	WAIT
15789 F87A 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     F87C AE2A     
15790 F87E A684     	data wait
15791               	; 	WAIT
15792 F880 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     F882 AE2A     
15793 F884 A684     	data wait
15794               	; 	WAIT
15795 F886 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     F888 AE2A     
15796 F88A A684     	data wait
15797               	; 	GOTO life_finish
15798 F88C 0460  28 	b @cvb_LIFE_FINISH
     F88E F86A     
15799               	;
15800               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
15801               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
15802               	; 	'
15803               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
15804               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
15805               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
15806               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
15807               	; 	'
15808               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
15809               	; 	'
15810               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
15811               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
15812               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
15813               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
15814               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
15815               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
15816               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
15817               	; 	'
15818               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
15819               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
15820               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
15821               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
15822               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15823               	; 	'
15824               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15825               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15826               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15827               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15828               	; 	#if TI994A
15829               	; 	BANK 2
15830      076E     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

16786               	;
16787               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- GAME MUSIC
16788               	; 	' CHASE (game_tune, genmusic.py) plays during a round on PLAY SIMPLE NO
16789               	; 	' DRUMS: TWO voices on channels 0 and 1 only. The TI effects split by
16790               	; 	' channel -- 0 the jump warble (swt), 1 hits and the escape (sht), 2
16791               	; 	' prizes/lives/tally, noise the footsteps -- so only jumps and hits
16792               	; 	' collide, and those DUCK the music: PLAY NONE freezes the player where
16793               	; 	' it is (it only clears music_mode; the song position is untouched), and
16794               	; 	' PLAY SIMPLE NO DRUMS resumes from the same note once they end.
16795               	; 	'
16796               	; 	' The test runs BEFORE sfx_tick writes anything, and counts the pending
16797               	; 	' latches (sfj/sfh/sfe) as well as the running counters, so the player
16798               	; 	' has let go of the channel before the effect's first write -- otherwise
16799               	; 	' the next vblank would stomp that first frame.
16800               	; 	'
16801               	; 	' Called from the main loop only, never from pause_beat: the round-end
16802               	; 	' pause is effects-only (pause_beat stops the music on entry).
16803               	; 	'
16804               	; 	' IT LIVES IN BANK 2 and the main loop maps bank 2 around the call: the
16805               	; 	' fixed area's UNOPTIMISED first pass had 156 bytes left and this body
16806               	; 	' did not fit. A bonus: PLAY game_tune runs with bank 2 already mapped,
16807               	; 	' which is the page the player records for the tune. Nothing here may
16808               	; 	' BANK SELECT (it would unmap itself).
16809               	; music_duck:
16810               cvb_MUSIC_DUCK
16811               	; 	IF musen = 0 THEN RETURN	' M on the title turned music off

16819               	; 	#if NES
16820               	; 	' NES RAM IS FULL TO THE BYTE, so the NES keeps no gms/gmp/gmb: its whole
16821               	; 	' music state is nai -- 0 playing, 1 ducked, 2 not started. nai is NES
16822               	; 	' scratch that is idle here: the title's A toggle uses it (and treats 2
16823               	; 	' like a held A), and the round-end message boxes use it only after the
16824               	; 	' round's music is over and before music_stop sets it back to 2.
16825               	; 	IF nai = 2 THEN nai = 0 : PLAY SIMPLE NO DRUMS : PLAY game_tune
16826               	; 	' Same test as below, branching instead of setting gmb, plus the channel
16827               	; 	' owners the NES adds (the bugle on 0, the prize on 1 -- nes_apu.asm).
16828               	; 	' ONE TEST, NOT NINE. Every one of these is an unsigned byte, so "any is
16829               	; 	' non-zero" is their bitwise OR: one load and eight ORAs, about 35
16830               	; 	' bytes, where nine `IF x > 0 THEN GOTO` cost about 105 on the 6502 --
16831               	; 	' part of what let the NES title play the whole of STREET. (A bitwise OR
16832               	; 	' of VALUES, not of comparisons, so the TI's AND/OR hazard does not
16833               	; 	' apply; and this block is NES-only anyway.)
16834               	; 	IF swt OR sht OR sfj OR sfh OR sfe OR spt OR spz OR sfk OR sfp THEN GOTO md_busy
16835               	; 	IF nai = 0 THEN RETURN

17137               	;
17138               	; 	' NO ALPHA LOCK CALIBRATION, AND THERE USED TO BE ONE.
17139               	; 	'
17140               	; 	' The premise was that ALPHA LOCK shares a line with the joystick's
17141               	; 	' VERTICAL axis, so a latched key reports a direction that is never
17142               	; 	' released -- fatal here, where down is the duck and up is the lift. The
17143               	; 	' guard sampled the axis for forty frames before listening and then
17144               	; 	' ignored any direction that had been held for essentially all of them.
17145               	; 	'
17146               	; 	' IT WAS REMOVED BECAUSE THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD UP.
17147               	; 	'
17148               	; 	'   * CLAUDE.md claimed every other game here dodged the problem by not
17149               	; 	'     reading up/down. EIGHT of them do read it -- Adventire, Astiroids,
17150               	; 	'     HardHatMack, Ms. Pac-Man, RallyX, Structris, UFO, Bust-A-Bobble --
17151               	; 	'     and not one has a calibration or has ever shown the fault.
17152               	; 	'   * It never fired on the machine this is developed on: the notice it
17153               	; 	'     prints when it detects a stuck axis has never appeared.
17154               	; 	'   * The original evidence was that the game "came up and would not
17155               	; 	'     start" -- and the first version BLOCKED until the axis cleared. That
17156               	; 	'     symptom is indistinguishable from the several input bugs since found
17157               	; 	'     and fixed for real: keys arriving at a screen that was not listening
17158               	; 	'     yet. The diagnosis was probably one of those.
17159               	; 	'
17160               	; 	' It also cost two bugs of its own: forty frames of a drawn but deaf title
17161               	; 	' screen, which swallowed the first digit of 8-3-8, and a wrong theory
17162               	; 	' about keyboard noise that led to a filter which ate real presses.
17163               	; 	'
17164               	; 	' If a stuck axis ever does appear it will be obvious -- the player will
17165               	; 	' duck or ride the lift without asking -- and the guard is in the history.

17261 699A A684     	data wait
17262               	; 	' THE MARQUEE CHASES WHILE THE TITLE WAITS.
17263               	; 	'
17264               	; 	' ONLY TWO CHARACTERS CHANGE PER STEP. At any moment exactly one of the
17265               	; 	' four lamps is blank; a step lights the one that was blank and blanks the
17266               	; 	' next one round. Redefining all four would be twice the work for the same
17267               	; 	' picture.
17268               	; 	'
17269               	; 	' IT IS BELOW THE INPUT READS, deliberately. This loop's history is input
17270               	; 	' bugs -- a screen that was drawn but not listening, a keypress eaten by a
17271               	; 	' stability filter -- so nothing that is merely decoration goes in front of
17272               	; 	' the polling. A dropped frame of animation is invisible; a dropped
17273               	; 	' keypress is what took three sessions to find.
17274               	; 	' `bphs` IS WHICH LAMP IS DARK, and a step is: light that one, move on,
17275               	; 	' darken the next. The character number is arithmetic rather than a
17276               	; 	' four-way branch -- DEFINE CHAR takes an expression, so the whole chase
17277               	; 	' is two calls and no `IF` ladder. The ladder version was eight DEFINE
17278               	; 	' CHARs across four branches and cost about three hundred bytes for the
17279               	; 	' same picture.
17280               	; 	'
17281               	; 	' TWO CALLS, NOT FIVE. Lighting all four and then darkening one is the
17282               	; 	' same result and reads more simply, but two separate DEFINEs can have a
17283               	; 	' vblank between them, so the sign would show ALL lamps lit for a frame
17284               	; 	' every step -- a flash rather than a chase. Only ever changing the two
17285               	; 	' lamps that actually change cannot do that.
17286               	; 	bfr = bfr - 1

17353               	; 		#if NES
17354               	; 		' A SECOND STAGING AREA, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE MARQUEE BUG.
17355               	; 		'
17356               	; 		' nes_escd does NOT copy anything. It builds the tile into the RAM
17357               	; 		' buffer `#nesb` and hands the NMI a five-byte descriptor holding a
17358               	; 		' POINTER to it; the copy happens at the next vblank. Both marquee
17359               	; 		' writes happen in the same pass, so with one buffer the darken call
17360               	; 		' overwrote the staged LIT bytes before the NMI had read either --
17361               	; 		' and then BOTH descriptors copied bulb_off.
17362               	; 		'
17363               	; 		' So every step darkened two lamps and lit none, and the sign walked
17364               	; 		' itself out: "it animates a little bit and goes out". Nothing fails,
17365               	; 		' because both writes are perfectly valid and land exactly where they
17366               	; 		' were addressed -- they just carry the same sixteen bytes.
17367               	; 		'

17611               	;
17612               	; 	' 8-3-8 IS EDGE-TRIGGERED AND ANY STRAY DIGIT RESETS IT (see title_wait).
17613               	; 	'
17614               	; 	' It used to read cont1.key raw every pass and test only for the digit it
17615               	; 	' wanted next. That worked -- but only because 8-3-8 ALTERNATES, so holding
17616               	; 	' 8 cannot advance past the first step. It is an accident of the sequence
17617               	; 	' rather than a design, and it had two costs: 8,5,3,9,8 opened this page as
17618               	; 	' readily as 8,3,8, and a key that READS as held for many frames got a free
17619               	; 	' walk through the state machine.
17620               	; 	'
17621               	; 	' That second one is not hypothetical on this machine. ALPHA LOCK shorts a
17622               	; 	' keyboard line -- and Classic99 defaults to invertcaps, so it reads DOWN
17623               	; 	' with the host's Caps Lock UP -- and this page was reached twice from
17624               	; 	' single keypresses while testing an unrelated change.
17625               	; 	'
17626               	; 	' The reset is the DEFAULT rather than a test for a particular wrong digit:
17627               	; 	' Bust-A-Bobble resets only on a stray 3 and still lets 8,5,3,8 through.
17628               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------------- 838 setup page
17629               	; 	' ======================================================================
17630               	; 	' A NEW GAME / A NEW KROOK
17631               	; 	' ======================================================================
17632               	;
17633               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- MOVED TO BANK 2
17634               	; 	' setup_font and init_tables run ONCE, at power-on, and read nothing from
17635               	; 	' bank 1 -- so on the TI they live here, in bank 2, and the caller selects
17636               	; 	' bank 2 around the GOSUB. They moved to make room for the TI music player
17637               	; 	' (title music, ~1.2 KB of runtime in the fixed area): with it, the
17638               	; 	' UNOPTIMISED first assembly ran past >FFFF and xas99 rejected branches
17639               	; 	' before shortbranches.py could run (CLAUDE.md 3A, TI short-branch note).
17640               	; 	' A routine placed here must not BANK SELECT (it would unmap itself) and
17641               	; 	' must not read bank 1: init_tables' one bank-1 read, jarc_tbl, stayed
17642               	; 	' behind as init_jarc. On ColecoVision and NES this is ordinary code.
17643               	; setup_font:
17644               cvb_SETUP_FONT
17645               	; 	' Flicker stays OFF. CVBasic's is all-or-nothing -- it rotates all 32
17646               	; 	' slots, so Kelly would strobe too, and he is the one thing the player
17647               	; 	' must never lose. He is sprite 0 instead: the VDP drops the
17648               	; 	' HIGHEST-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so slot 0 is the
17649               	; 	' one slot that can never disappear.
17650               	; 	SPRITE FLICKER OFF

17674               	;
17675               	; 	#if NES
17676               	; 	' THE NES'S TWO STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES, SETTLED ONCE, HERE.
17677               	; 	'
17678               	; 	' 1. WHERE THE PATTERNS LIVE. In 8x16 sprite mode the sprite pattern table
17679               	; 	'    is chosen by bit 0 of each OAM tile byte and the PPUCTRL bit is
17680               	; 	'    ignored -- and every pattern number in this game is a multiple of
17681               	; 	'    four, so that bit is always 0 and the sprites are nailed to $0000.
17682               	; 	'    nes_bgbank therefore moves the BACKGROUND to $1000 rather than trying
17683               	; 	'    to move the sprites, which also lands the background patterns at
17684               	; 	'    address 4096, exactly where the TMS bitmap mode's third screen third
17685               	; 	'    had them -- so the radar's pattern writes need a stride and nothing
17686               	; 	'    else.
17687               	; 	'
17688               	; 	' 2. COLOUR DOES NOT MAP AND IS NOT PRETENDED TO. The NES colours in 16x16
17689               	; 	'    attribute blocks; this game colours per character, two colours a
17690               	; 	'    cell. So the store is drawn in ONE ink and the actors get four
17691               	; 	'    palettes, picked by the low two bits of the colour argument the
17692               	; 	'    SPRITE statements already pass -- 1 (black) -> dark grey, 4/8 (blue)
17693               	; 	'    -> blue, 14 (grey) -> grey, 11/15 (skin, white) -> white. Nothing in
17694               	; 	'    the game source has to know.
17695               	; 	ASM JSR nes_bgbank
17696               	; 	ASM JSR nes_apuon
17697               	;
17698               	; 	' Grey is shared index 0 during gameplay. Other indices are per region.
17699               	; 	' gennescolor.py assigns P3 only to counter quadrants, retaining green
17700               	; 	' wall and gold floor colours. Fixtures with black outlines use P0.
17701               	; 	PALETTE 1,26			' P0: green, black, gold
17702               	; 	PALETTE 2,15			' black escalators and fixture outlines
17703               	; 	PALETTE 3,40
17704               	; 	PALETTE 5,1			' P1 HUD/upper skyline: blue, pink, gold
17705               	; 	PALETTE 6,36
17706               	; 	PALETTE 7,40
17707               	; 	PALETTE 9,38			' P2 lower skyline: orange, black, gold
17708               	; 	PALETTE 10,1			' unused skyline index 2: navy message bottom border
17709               	; 	PALETTE 11,40
17710               	; 	PALETTE 13,26			' P3 counters: green, blue, gold
17711               	; 	PALETTE 14,1			' same navy in counter quadrants
17712               	; 	PALETTE 15,40
17713               	;
17714               	; 	' AND FOUR FOR THE ACTORS, which DO get one each because a sprite carries
17715               	; 	' its own palette number. nes_spal maps the TMS colour every SPRITE
17716               	; 	' statement already passes onto these four.
17717               	; 	PALETTE 17,18			' 0 -- blue   Kelly's trousers
17718               	; 	PALETTE 21,15			' 1 -- black  hats, Harry's stripes, the Kop's dot.
17719               	; 					' FIFTEEN, NOT ZERO: on this palette $0F is
17720               	; 					' black and $00 is a dark GREY, so every hat
17721               	; 					' and every stripe was coming out grey.
17722               	; 	PALETTE 22,23			' black sprite palette, index 2: brown suitcase outline
17723               	; 	PALETTE 25,39			' 2 -- skin   faces and the biplane
17724               	; 	PALETTE 26,16			' 2 colour 2 -- GREY, the lift car on the radar
17725               	; 	' AND THE BALL IS RED, which it already is on the TI: C_BALL is TMS 8,
17726               	; 	' medium red. nes_spal sends that to sprite palette 2, and palette 2's
17727               	; 	' colour ONE is the skin tone -- so on this machine the ball came out the
17728               	; 	' same pale orange as a face.
17729               	; 	'
17730               	; 	' A sprite here is ONE bitplane, so its pixels are whichever index the
17731               	; 	' upload writes and the OAM byte only chooses the palette. The lift car on
17732               	; 	' the radar already solved this: it is uploaded with `nink = 2` and reads
17733               	; 	' palette 2's second entry. The ball does the same with the THIRD, which
17734               	; 	' nothing else uses.
17735               	; 	PALETTE 27,22			' 2 colour 3 -- RED, the bouncing balls
17736               	; 	PALETTE 29,48			' 3 -- white  Harry, the carts, the lift car
17737               	;
17738               	; 	#endif
17739               	; 	#if TI994A
17740               	; 	#else
17741               	; 	nespw = 2			' NES/Coleco start on a 2-frame pass
17742               	; 	#endif
17743               	;
17744               	; 	' THE ONE AND ONLY BANK SWITCH THE PROGRAM EVER MAKES, and it happens
17745               	; 	' here, before the first frame.
17746               	; 	'
17747               	; 	' There are two data banks now. Bank 1 holds everything read while the
17748               	; 	' game is running -- sprite and store art, the templates, the lookup
17749               	; 	' tables -- and it is selected at the end of this routine and never
17750               	; 	' changed again, so every VARPTR/PEEK read in the program is reading a
17751               	; 	' page that is permanently mapped. That is the property that makes
17752               	; 	' banking safe here: a missed BANK SELECT returns bytes from the wrong
17753               	; 	' page with no error at build or run time, so the safest number of
17754               	; 	' switches during play is none.
17755               	; 	'
17756               	; 	' Bank 2 exists to hold data that is read ONCE, at setup, and never
17757               	; 	' again. The font is exactly that: two DEFINEs copy it into VRAM and
17758               	; 	' nothing reads font_bits or font_col for the rest of the run. So it can
17759               	; 	' live on a page that is mapped for the length of those two statements.
17760               	; 	'
17761               	; 	' IF THIS EVER FAILS IT FAILS LOUDLY. Select the wrong bank here and the
17762               	; 	' font is garbage on the title screen, immediately and unmistakably --
17763               	; 	' which is the same diagnostic the font used to provide by staying out of
17764               	; 	' the banks altogether, recovered for free.
17765               	;
17766               	; 	#if NES
17767               	; 	' THE FONT IS SENT WITH A COLOUR TABLE SO ITS PAPER IS NOT THE BACKDROP.
17768               	; 	'
17769               	; 	' With `#ncol = 0` the uploader puts ink `nink` on index 0 -- the UNIVERSAL
17770               	; 	' backdrop, black in the game -- so every character of text sat in its own
17771               	; 	' black box. The score line was a black strip across the top of a blue sky.
17772               	; 	'
17773               	; 	' Index 0 cannot be set per region (it is one colour for the whole screen),
17774               	; 	' so the only way to give text a ground is to put its PAPER on another
17775               	; 	' index, and paper is written into the second bitplane when the character
17776               	; 	' is uploaded. Hence a table: $B4 is light yellow on dark blue, which
17777               	; 	' nes_inkmap sends to index 3 and index 1.
17778               	; 	'
17779               	; 	' ONE FONT, NOT TWO. The first attempt at this made a SECOND copy of the
17780               	; 	' font at codes 197.. so the HUD could differ from the message boxes, and
17781               	; 	' that was both unnecessary and impossible: in game the HUD and the boxes
17782               	; 	' are the same text and want the same treatment, and 197..207 is only
17783               	; 	' ELEVEN free codes -- 208 up is the radar canvas (genart's SCAN_FIRST),
17784               	; 	' which scan_wipe rewrites as raw pattern memory every frame. The 59-char
17785               	; 	' copy appeared to upload and was scribbled over from its twelfth character
17786               	; 	' on. See checkpat.py, which now knows the canvas owns those codes.
17787               	; 	'
17788               	; 	' What index 1 IS comes from the attribute table, per region: the HUD row
17789               	; 	' is on P1 (dark blue, below) and the store is on P0.
17790               	; 	#nsrc = VARPTR font_bits(0)
17791               	; 	nchr = 32
17792               	; 	ncnt = 59
17793               	; 	ntab = 1
17794               	; 	' THE FONT'S COLOUR, $B4 on every row of all 59 characters: light yellow
17795               	; 	' on dark blue, ink index 3 on paper index 1, and which colours those are
17796               	; 	' is then the attribute table's business, per region. It used to be a
17797               	; 	' 472-byte table of that one value (nes_fcol), kept because "ROM is not
17798               	; 	' the scarce budget" -- on the NES it is. A #ncol under $100 is the
17799               	; 	' colour byte itself (assets/nes_chr.asm, nes_chrinkrow).
17800               	; 	#ncol = $B4
17801               	; 	nink = 3
17802               	; 	GOSUB nes_def
17803               	; 	#else

17805 6B94 0204  20 	li r4,32
     6B96 0020     
17806 6B98 0205  20 	li r5,15104
     6B9A 3B00

     6B9E 6D34     
17808 6BA0 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     6BA2 AE2A

17810               	; 	#endif
17811               	; 	' Without this the font keeps whatever CVBasic left in the colour table --
17812               	; 	' white on transparent -- which over a green store made the HUD unreadable.
17813               	; 	'
17814               	; 	' THIS WAS A VPOKE LOOP AND IT WAS THE SLOWEST THING IN THE BOOT: 1,416
17815               	; 	' writes of one constant, paced by 24 WAITs, which is what made the title
17816               	; 	' fill in visibly instead of appearing. DEFINE COLOR does the same job in a
17817               	; 	' single call with interrupts off, and it writes all three screen thirds
17818               	; 	' itself -- define_color always takes the LDIRVM3 triple-copy path, which is
17819               	; 	' also why esc_deck_col and floor0_colour below CANNOT use it: they patch
17820               	; 	' one third each.
17821               	; 	'
17822               	; 	' The table is 472 identical bytes (genfont.py emits it beside the glyphs).
17823               	; 	' It reads as waste and is not: it lives in the data bank, which had 860
17824               	; 	' bytes spare, while the loop it replaced cost time in the one place the
17825               	; 	' player is made to wait.
17826               	; 	#if NES

17828               	; 	#else

18073               	; 	' DESIGN.md 5a depends on the apex being exactly 14.
18074               	; 	'

18076               	; 	' frames that touched 14 for only four, which made every jump a timing
18077               	; 	' test rather than a decision -- you had to leave the ground on exactly
18078               	; 	' the right frame or clip the thing you were jumping. Widening the
18079               	; 	' plateau rather than raising the apex keeps the ball arithmetic in

18081               	; 	' window forgiving: the player still has to CHOOSE to jump, but no longer
18082               	; 	' has to be frame-perfect about it.

18116 6D30 C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
18117 6D32 0450  20 	b *r0
18118               	;
18119               	; 	' THE FONT'S COLOUR TABLE WAS 472 BYTES OF ONE REPEATED VALUE, which is a
18120               	; 	' fifth of what the fixed area had left. DEFINE COLOR copies such a table
18121               	; 	' out of ROM into all three screen thirds; writing the constant straight
18122               	; 	' into the colour table does the same job for the price of a loop, and
18123               	; 	' the loop runs once, at boot.
18124               	; 	'
18125               	; 	' The colour table is at >2000 and the VDP mirrors it once per screen
18126               	; 	' third, >800 apart. Both numbers were read out of the GENERATED assembly
18127               	; 	' -- define_color's `ai r0,>2000` and LDIRVM3's `ai r0,>0800` -- rather
18128               	; 	' than assumed, because a wrong base here would paint over the pattern
18129               	; 	' table and the failure would look like corrupt artwork.
18130               	; 	'
18131               	; 	' Paced: a few hundred VDP writes in one frame are silently dropped.
18132               	; 	' THE SCANNER'S COLOURS ARE THREE BLOCKS REPEATED SIXTEEN TIMES EACH, so
18133               	; 	' the table shipped 384 bytes to say 24 bytes' worth. Same trick as the
18134               	; 	' font: write the colour table directly. >2000 is the colour table's base
18135               	; 	' and >800 the stride between screen thirds -- the same layout DEFINE COLOR
18136               	; 	' walks for us in setup_font, which this cannot use because it is cheaper to
18137               	; 	' expand 24 bytes here than to ship 384 in the bank.
18138               	; 	' NOTHING IS UNDER THE GROUND FLOOR, SO NOTHING SHOULD BE GREEN THERE.
18139               	; 	' A floor bar is five pixels of yellow over three of the green air
18140               	; 	' belonging to the floor BELOW it (see SLAB), which is right for three of
18141               	; 	' the four bars and wrong for the last one: below floor 0 there is no
18142               	; 	' floor, only the scanner, and the green read as a strip of shop with
18143               	; 	' nothing in it.
18144               	; 	'
18145               	; 	' NO NEW CHARACTER IS NEEDED, BECAUSE THE COLOUR TABLE HAS THREE COPIES
18146               	; 	' -- one per eight screen rows -- and the bands land such that each bar
18147               	; 	' sits in a different third:
18148               	; 	'
18149               	; 	'     band 0 roof   rows  1-5    bar row  5   third 0
18150               	; 	'     band 1        rows  6-10   bar row 10   third 1
18151               	; 	'     band 2        rows 11-15   bar row 15   third 1
18152               	; 	'     band 3 GROUND rows 16-20   bar row 20   third 2
18153               	; 	'
18154               	; 	' so recolouring SLAB in third 2 alone reaches the ground floor's bar and
18155               	; 	' nothing else. The same third also holds the scanner, but the scanner
18156               	; 	' does not use these characters. This is the same mechanism that once hid
18157               	; 	' a bug for months (CLAUDE.md 3A, the blanked-in-one-third note) used
18158               	; 	' deliberately for once.
18159               	; 	'
18160               	; 	' Only the three bottom lines change, and only their BACKGROUND: SLAB has
18161               	; 	' no ink there and SLABE's brick keeps its grey.
18162               	;
18163               	; 	INCLUDE "font.bas"
18164               	; 	' Keystone Kapers font -- GENERATED by assets/genfont.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
18165               	; 	'
18166               	; 	' Characters 32-90 (59 of them), 8 bytes each = 472 bytes. Williams' cabinet face:
18167               	; 	' heavy, squared, flat terminals, no serifs -- drawn 5x7 inside the 8x8 cell so a
18168               	; 	' blank column at the right and a blank row at the bottom keep it legible.
18169               	; 	'
18170               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE CHAR 32,59,font_bits. The run must be CONTIGUOUS, so slots
18171               	; 	' with no glyph emit blanks rather than being skipped -- a gap would shift every
18172               	; 	' letter after it.
18173               	;
18174               	; font_bits:
18175               cvb_FONT_BITS

18294               	;
18295               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($B4 = light yellow ink on dark blue).
18296               	; 	'
18297               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
18298               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
18299               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
18300               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
18301               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
18302               	; 	'
18303               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
18304               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
18305               	;
18306               	; #if NES
18307               	; 	' NES uses nes_fcol; omit this identical 472-byte TMS colour table.
18308               	; #else
18309               	; font_col:
18310               cvb_FONT_COL

18640               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY LIST, for the same reason as the font: walked
18641               	; 	' once by title_draw, at boot and on a return to the title, and never
18642               	; 	' during play. title_draw selects bank 2 around its walk.
18643               	; 	'
18644               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
18645               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
18646               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
18647               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
18648               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
18649               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
18650               	; 	' scan_cols is the TMS radar's colour table; its one reader, the DEFINE
18651               	; 	' COLOR in the non-NES setup path, does not exist on the NES, so neither

20623               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
20624               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
20625               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
20626               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
20627               	;
20628               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
20629               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
20630               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
20631               	; 	' unreadable.
20632               	;
20633               	; esc_deck:	' 6 x (char, 8 colour bytes) -- write into the THIRD-0 colour table at 8192 + char*8, once, at setup
20634               cvb_ESC_DECK

20741               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
20742               	; 	'
20743               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
20744               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
20745               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
20746               	; 	'
20747               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
20748               	; 	' blit is
20749               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
20750               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
20751               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
20752               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
20753               	; 	'
20754               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
20755               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
20756               	; 	'
20757               	; 	' template ids:
20758               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
20759               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B

21323               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- LZSS (TI)
21324               	; 	' THE DECODER for assets/lzss.py's format: a flag byte governs eight items,
21325               	; 	' least significant bit first; 1 = a literal byte, 0 = a two-byte match,
21326               	; 	' big-endian (offset << 4 | length - 3), offset 1..4095 back into the
21327               	; 	' output. #lzs = the compressed stream, #lzd = the RAM destination, #lzn =
21328               	; 	' the output length (it stops there, so a stream's padding is never read).
21329               	; 	' R1-R9 only: R10 is CVBasic's stack pointer and R11 its return link.
21330               	; 	' It lives in BANK 1 with its stream, which must be selected (power-on
21331               	; 	' selects it before calling lz_probe), and needs no fixed-area room.
21332               	; 	#if TI994A
